To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have studied the scaling properties of the charm and bottom sectors of QCD with a relativistic heavy quark action, and that we have found that the scaling violations of the heavy-quark sector of QCD are much smaller than those of the light sector, and that the scaling violations can be reduced to the level that is acceptable for phenomenological studies of heavy-quark hadrons.

we have successfully simulated the bottom system in lattice QCD using a relativistic heavy quark action and have obtained the mass spectrum of the bottomonium system and the decay constants of the pseudoscalar and vector bottom mesons.
we have performed quenched scaling studies of charm and bottom systems with a nonperturbatively renormalized relativistic heavy quark action.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of heavy quark systems in quenched QCD using the relativistic heavy quark action.
a quenched lattice QCD study of heavy quarks, with the aim of understanding the heavy quark mass dependence of the static potential, and of the static interquark potential.
the non-perturbative aspects of QCD, and the numerical simulations of lattice QCD are the most reliable tool to explore them.

we have found that the quark action of Ref. [1] is a good choice for the study of the heavy quark sector, at least in the quenched approximation.
the quenched scaling study with the relativistic heavy quark action is successful.

the quenched charm and bottom systems with a relativistic heavy quark action are well described by the scaling behavior of the continuum theory, and that the quenched bottomonium system is well described by a nonperturbatively improved action.
we have studied the quenched QCD at β = 6.0 with a relativistic heavy quark action.
